title: Priv: VPC IAM Role Patterns Generator and Least-Privilege Policy Compiler
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Private/VPC deployments require carefully scoped IAM to meet customer regulatory needs and internal least-privilege goals. Current terraform modules are manually curated and drift-prone; teams routinely over-provision roles to unblock deploys. Goal: build a generator that compiles role patterns from workload manifests and outputs a testable, least-privilege Terraform IAM module + a small policy minimizer that strips unused actions. The generator should integrate into CI to produce deterministic TF artifacts, support safe upgrades, and emit a human-friendly upgrade playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Generator accepts workload manifest (YAML) and outputs a reproducible Terraform module (roles, policies, bindings) that passes 'terraform plan' with no unexpected permissions
Generated policies must not contain obvious wildcards (e.g., iam:* where avoidable) and must be mechanically minimized against a static action map
CI job runs generator and fails merges if 'simulated-apply' shows new privileges beyond an approved delta
Upgrade playbook created that describes safe rollout steps for IAM changes including canary binding, audit log checks, and rollback commands
Integration tests using LocalStack (or equivalent) validate role binding flow and a simulated workload exercising a subset of actions
Security sign-off (internal security team) recorded in ticket comments before merging into main modules repo
tasks: Design DSL for role pattern templates (workload -> role affinity mapping)
Implement generator prototype in Go (CLI) to parse manifests and emit TF HCL v2 files
Add policy minimizer that intersects requested actions with known service action lists and removes unused ones
Create terraform module wrapper that supports namespacing, version pinning, and outputting metadata for audit
Add CI pipeline: generate -> terraform init/plan -> simulated-apply -> diff guard
Write integration tests using LocalStack for key AWS interactions (sts:AssumeRole, iam:PassRole, s3/get/put)
Author upgrade playbook and safe rollout runbook (canary binding, monitor metrics, rollback)
Security review and external audit checklist prep
Documentation: Confluence design spec, example manifests, and quickstart for platform engineers
notes: We aim for generator output to be deterministic and pin TF provider versions to avoid plan noise
Prefer least-privilege by default; provide an escape hatch label 'operational:allow-bypass' that requires approval
Design decision: minimize external API calls at generation time (use static action catalog bundled with releases) to be usable offline in air-gapped installs
Consider adding a 'policy simulation' toggle that runs against a staging account for higher-confidence validations for enterprise installs
